1.text: Tha song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
Let him kiss me wit tha kisses of his mouth: 4 ur love is better than wine.
Because of tha savour of ur good ointments ur name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do tha virgins love u.
Draw me, we will run after u: tha king has brought me in2 his chambers: we will be glad N rejoice in u, we will remember ur love more than wine: tha upright love u.
I am black, but comely, O y’all daughters of Jerusalem, as tha tents of Kedar, as tha curtains of Solomon.
Look not upon me, because I am black, because tha sun has looked upon me: my mother’s children were angry wit me; dey made me tha keeper of tha vineyards; but my own vineyard have I not kept.
Tell me, O u whom my soul loves, where u feed, where u make ur flock 2 rest at noon: 4 why should I be as one dat turns aside by tha flocks of ur companions?
If u know not, O u fairest among women, go ur way forth by tha footsteps of tha flock, N feed ur kids beside tha shepherds’ tents.
I have compared u, O my love, 2 a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.
Ur cheeks r comely wit rows of jewels, ur neck wit chains of gold.
We will make u borders of gold wit studs of silver.
While tha king sits at his table, my spikenard sends forth tha smell of it.
A bundle of myrrh is my wellbeloved 2 me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
My beloved is 2 me as a cluster of camphire in tha vineyards of En-gedi.
Look, u r fair, my love; look, u r fair; u have doves’ eyes.
Look, u r fair, my beloved, yeah, pleasant: also our bed is green.
Tha beams of our house r cedar, N our rafters of fir.

2.text: I am tha rose of Sharon, N tha lily of tha valleys.
As tha lily among thorns, so is my love among tha daughters.
As tha apple tree among tha trees of tha wood, so is my beloved among tha sons. I sat down under his shadow wit great delight, N his fruit was sweet 2 my taste.
He brought me 2 tha banqueting house, N his banner over me was love.
Stay me wit flagons, comfort me wit apples: 4 I am sick of love.
His left hand is under my head, N his right hand does embrace me.
I charge u, O y’all daughters of Jerusalem, by tha roes, N by tha hinds of tha field, dat y’all stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
Tha voice of my beloved! look, he comes leaping upon tha mountains, skipping upon tha hills.
My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: look, he stands behind our wall, he looks forth at tha windows, shewing himself through tha lattice.
My beloved spoke, N said 2 me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, N come away.
4, look, tha winter is past, tha rain is over N gone;
Tha flowers appear on tha earth; tha time of tha singin of birds is come, N tha voice of tha turtle is heard in our land;
Tha fig tree puts forth her green figs, N tha vines wit tha tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, N come away.
O my dove, dat art in tha clefts of tha rock, in tha secret places of tha stairs, let me see ur countenance, let me hear ur voice; 4 sweet is ur voice, N ur countenance is comely.
Take us tha foxes, tha little foxes, dat spoil tha vines: 4 our vines have tender grapes.
My beloved is mine, N I am his: he feeds among tha lilies.
Until tha day break, N tha shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, N be u like a roe or a young hart upon tha mountains of Bether.

3.text: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
I will rise now, N go about tha city in tha streets, N in tha broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.
Tha watchmen dat go about tha city found me: 2 whom I said, Saw y’all him whom my soul loves?

It was but a little dat I passed from ’em, but I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, N would not let him go, until I had brought him in2 my mother’s house, N in2 tha chamber of her dat conceived me.
I charge u, O y’all daughters of Jerusalem, by tha roes, N by tha hinds of tha field, dat y’all stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
Who is dis dat comes out of tha wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed wit myrrh N frankincense, wit all powders of tha merchant?
Look his bed, which is Solomon’s; threescore valiant men r about it, of tha valiant of Israel.
Dey all hold swords, bein expert in war: every man has his sword upon his thigh because of fear in tha night.
King Solomon made himself a chariot of tha wood of Lebanon.
He made tha pillars of it of silver, tha bottom of it of gold, tha covering of it of purple, tha midst of it bein paved wit love, 4 tha daughters of Jerusalem.
Go forth, O y’all daughters of Zion, N look king Solomon wit tha crown wherewith his mother crowned him in tha day of his espousals, N in tha day of tha gladness of his heart.

4.text: Look, u r fair, my love; look, u r fair; u have doves’ eyes within ur locks: ur hair is as a flock of goats, dat appear from mount Gilead.
Ur teeth r like a flock of sheep dat r even shorn, which came up from tha washing; whereof every one bear twins, N none is barren among ’em.
Ur lips r like a thread of scarlet, N ur speech is comely: ur temples r like a piece of a pomegranate within ur locks.
Ur neck is like tha tower of David builded 4 an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
Ur two breasts r like two young roes dat r twins, which feed among tha lilies.
Until tha day break, N tha shadows flee away, I will get me 2 tha mountain of myrrh, N 2 tha hill of frankincense.
u r all fair, my love; there is no spot in u.
Come wit me from Lebanon, my spouse, wit me from Lebanon: look from tha top of Amana, from tha top of Shenir N Hermon, from tha lions’ dens, from tha mountains of tha leopards.
u have ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; u have ravished my heart wit one of ur eyes, wit one chain of ur neck.
How fair is ur love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is ur love than wine! N tha smell of thine ointments than all spices!
Ur lips, O my spouse, drop as tha honeycomb: honey N milk r under ur tongue; N tha smell of ur garments is like tha smell of Lebanon.
A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
Ur plants r an orchard of pomegranates, wit pleasant fruits; camphire, wit spikenard,
Spikenard N saffron; calamus N cinnamon, wit all trees of frankincense; myrrh N aloes, wit all tha chief spices:
A fountain of gardens, a well of livin waterz, N streams from Lebanon.
Awake, O north wind; N come, u south; blow upon my garden, dat tha spices of it may flow out. Let my beloved come in2 his garden, N eat his pleasant fruits.

5.text: I am come in2 my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh wit my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb wit my honey; I have drunk my wine wit my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yeah, drink abundantly, O beloved.

I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is tha voice of my beloved dat knocketh, sayin, Open 2 me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: 4 my head is filled wit dew, N my locks wit tha drops of tha night.
I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile ’em?
My beloved put in his hand by tha hole of tha door, N my bowels were moved 4 him.
I rose up 2 open 2 my beloved; N my hands dropped wit myrrh, N my fingers wit sweet smelling myrrh, upon tha handles of tha lock.
I opened 2 my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, N was gone: my soul failed when he spoke: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
Tha watchmen dat went about tha city found me, dey struck me, dey wounded me; tha keepers of tha walls took away my veil from me.
I charge u, O daughters of Jerusalem, if y’all find my beloved, dat y’all tell him, dat I am sick of love.
What is ur beloved more than another beloved, O u fairest among women? what is ur beloved more than another beloved, dat u do so charge us?
My beloved is white N ruddy, tha chiefest among ten thousand.
His head is as tha most fine gold, his locks r bushy, N black as a raven.
His eyes r as tha eyes of doves by tha rivers of waterz, washed wit milk, N fitly set.
His cheeks r as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
His hands r as gold rings set wit tha beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid wit sapphires.
His legs r as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as tha cedars.
His mouth is most sweet: yeah, he is altogether lovely. dis is my beloved, N dis is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

6.text: Where is ur beloved gone, O u fairest among women? where is ur beloved turned aside? dat we may seek him wit u.
My beloved is gone down in2 his garden, 2 tha beds of spices, 2 feed in tha gardens, N 2 gather lilies.
I am my beloved’s, N my beloved is mine: he feeds among tha lilies.
u r beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army wit banners.
Turn away ur eyes from me, 4 dey have overcome me: ur hair is as a flock of goats dat appear from Gilead.
Ur teeth r as a flock of sheep which go up from tha washing, whereof every one bears twins, N there is not one barren among ’em.
As a piece of a pomegranate r ur temples within ur locks.
There r threescore queens, N fourscore concubines, N virgins without number.

My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is tha only one of her mother, she is tha choice one of her dat bare her. tha daughters saw her, N blessed her; yeah, tha queens N tha concubines, N dey praised her.
Who is she dat looks forth as tha morning, fair as tha moon, clear as tha sun, N terrible as an army wit banners?
I went down in2 tha garden of nuts 2 see tha fruits of tha valley, N 2 see whether tha vine flourished, N tha pomegranates budded.
Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like tha chariots of Amminadib.
Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, dat we may look upon u. What will y’all see in tha Shulamite? As it were tha company of two armies.

7.text: How beautiful r ur feet wit shoes, O prince’s daughter! tha joints of ur thighs r like jewels, tha work of tha hands of a cunning workman.
Ur navel is like a round goblet, which wants not liquor: ur belly is like an heap of wheat set about wit lilies.
Ur two breasts r like two young roes dat r twins.
Ur neck is as a tower of ivory; ur eyes like tha fishpools in Heshbon, by tha gate of Bath-rabbim: ur nose is as tha tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
Thine head upon u is like Carmel, N tha hair of thine head like purple; tha king is held in tha galleries.
How fair N how pleasant r u, O love, 4 delights!
Dis ur stature is like 2 a palm tree, N ur breasts 2 clusters of grapes.
I said, I will go up 2 tha palm tree, I will take hold of tha boughs of it: now also ur breasts shall be as clusters of tha vine, N tha smell of ur nose like apples;
N tha roof of ur mouth like tha best wine 4 my beloved, dat goes down sweetly, causing tha lips of dose dat r asleep 2 speak.
I am my beloved’s, N his desire is toward me.
Come, my beloved, let us go forth in2 tha field; let us lodge in tha villages.
Let us get up early 2 tha vineyards; let us see if tha vine flourish, whether tha tender grape appear, N tha pomegranates bud forth: there will I give u my loves.
Tha mandrakes give a smell, N at our gates r all manner of pleasant fruits, new N old, which I have laid up 4 u, O my beloved.

8.text: O dat u were as my brother, dat sucked tha breasts of my mother! when I should find u without, I would kiss u; yeah, I should not be despised.
I would lead u, N bring u in2 my mother’s house, who would instruct me: I would cause u 2 drink of spiced wine of tha juice of my pomegranate.
His left hand should be under my head, N his right hand should embrace me.
I charge u, O daughters of Jerusalem, dat y’all stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.
Who is dis dat comes up from tha wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised u up under tha apple tree: there ur mother brought u forth: there she brought u forth dat bare u.
Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: 4 love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as tha grave: tha coals of it r coals of fire, which has a most vehement flame.
Many waterz cannot quench love, neither can tha floods drown it: if a man would give all tha substance of his house 4 love, it would utterly be contemned.
We have a little sister, N she has no breasts: what shall we do 4 our sister in tha day when she shall be spoken 4?
If she be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: N if she be a door, we will inclose her wit boards of cedar.
I am a wall, N my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one dat found favour.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out tha vineyard 2 keepers; every one 4 tha fruit of it was 2 bring a thousand pieces of silver.
My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: u, O Solomon, must have a thousand, N dose dat keep tha fruit of it two hundred.
u dat dwell in tha gardens, tha companions listen 2 ur voice: cause me 2 hear it.
Make haste, my beloved, N be u like 2 a roe or 2 a young hart upon tha mountains of spices.
